title.narrative: Enhancing protection of rights and freedoms of vulnerable communities in regard to; land access, ownership and utilization among the refugees and host communities of Northern Uganda

description.narrative:
This Action has been prepared by KRC-Uganda in partnership with Centre for Social Cultural Rights Africa (CESCRA) and Women and Rural Development Network (WORUDET) and in full consultation with the contacts from the communities in the three refugee settlements and the host communities. This was done with assistance from the contacts of the on-going project in the three settlements (Palabek, Rhino and Bidibidi) run by the same partners and from local leadership who were consulted in various periodic review meetings. Furthermore, a number of studies have been conducted to identify the missing gap that will be filled by this action within the three refugee settlements. These studies included; the baseline study (2021), contextual analysis (2021) and the Mid-term project evaluation (2023).


Uganda remains one of the leading countries hosting refugees in Africa and third world over with a total refugee population of 1,532,168 (UNHCR, March 2023) with women and children making 80% of the total refugee population. Uganda operates a settlement approach which makes its refugee policies accommodative where refugees are availed with land use rights for settlement and economic self-reliance. Therefore, refugees are permitted freedom of movement, legal employment, access to markets and user rights to be allocated plots of land as means to economic freedom. However, Uganda¿s refugee policy fails to address land negotiations and acquisition and pre-construction. The settlement¿s physical layout has often times resulted into disagreements that lead to conflict between the refugees and the host communities.
